## The Core Claim

The real geometric constraints in Rosalind Franklin's X-ray diffraction pattern (Photo 51) -- a helical pitch of ~34 angstroms, ~10 base pairs per turn, uniform diameter -- uniquely constrain the chemical structure of DNA to a double helix with complementary base pairing (adenine-thymine, guanine-cytosine), independently consistent with Chargaff's ratios. That structure then correctly predicted semi-conservative replication, confirmed by the Meselson-Stahl experiment (1958) -- a real, distinct, independently-tested consequence of the same structural model. Watson, Crick, and Wilkins won the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for this.
